definition: A degenerative process where a model trained repeatedly on data generated by earlier AI models (rather than diverse human-generated data) loses diversity and quality over successive generations.
details: Model collapse is a growing concern as more AI-generated content appears on the web and potentially gets swept into future training datasets, motivating interest in provenance tracking and careful data curation.

explainer.lead: A degenerative process in which a model trained repeatedly on data generated by earlier AI models, rather than diverse human data, loses diversity and quality across successive generations. It matters increasingly as AI-generated content spreads on the web and risks entering future training data.

tiers.eli5: If you keep photocopying a photocopy, each copy gets blurrier until the details are gone.
tiers.practitioner: Concerns about collapse motivate provenance tracking and careful data curation of training corpora. A pitfall is letting generated content silently contaminate datasets without provenance checks.
tiers.paperLevel: Repeated training on model-generated rather than diverse human data degrades diversity and quality over generations; mitigation relies on provenance tracking and curation.

explainer.example: A series of models each trained on the previous generation's outputs shows shrinking diversity and falling quality.
